reason: The cited evidence supports that active-learning ML potentials achieve near-DFT accuracy for refractory multicomponent alloys (E1, E2) and enable larger-scale simulations, but neither passage addresses free-energy calculations, thermodynamic integration, or the capture of electron–vibration coupling. The key premises about free-energy fidelity and adaptive corrections for electron–vibration coupling are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: ML potentials trained on ab initio data can reach near-DFT accuracy for multicomponent alloys
Active learning tailors the training set to the target system and properties, improving accuracy over fixed training sets
ML potentials enable larger supercells and longer simulations than DFT, reducing computational cost
Thermodynamic integration on an ML potential surface yields reliable free energies including vibrational and anharmonic contributions
Adaptive ab initio corrections can capture subtle electron–vibration coupling effects in critical regions
